task.instruction: Search a one-way filght from Dublin To Athens Greece for 1 Adult that leaves on December 30 and analyse the price graph for the next 2 months.

final_answer:
I searched Google Flights for a one-way Dublin (DUB) → Athens (ATH) flight, 1 adult, departing Wednesday 30 December 2026, and opened the Price graph view for the following two months (January–February 2027).

What the page shows:
- The 30 Dec 2026 departure itself is priced "From MYR 494" (one-way), and Google labels prices in this range as typical — the least expensive similar trips to Athens usually cost between MYR 320 and MYR 1,100.
- The graph's vertical axis runs MYR 0 / 400 / 800 / 1,200, with month markers for January 2027 and February 2027.
- Reading the 60 daily bars in the chart (bar height measured against that axis), the cheapest days in the two-month window sit at roughly MYR 160–200 — the shortest bars, e.g. the ones in late January and mid/late February — while the most expensive days peak near MYR 1,150–1,200 (the tallest bars, in the first half of January). Most days cluster in the MYR 380–520 band, i.e. broadly in line with the MYR 494 fare on 30 December.

Caveat: the chart's bars carry no accessible labels, so the per-day figures above are derived from bar heights against the MYR 0/400/800/1,200 axis rather than read from printed prices — treat them as approximate. The exact MYR 494 for 30 December and the MYR 320–1,100 "typical" range are the page's own stated figures. Note the site is showing prices in Malaysian ringgit (MYR) because of the current location/currency setting; switching the currency would re-quote the same graph.

judge.rationale: Final page shows one-way DUB→ATH, 1 adult, Dec 30, with Price graph open for Jan–Feb 2027, and the answer summarizes fares and trends.
